claims.claim: Final sealed evaluation completed with qualification outcome 'qualified', status 'completed', correct true (integrity of measurement, not support for the hypothesis).
Slope of ln(delay) on log2(width) is -0.020 (point estimate).
95% seed-cluster bootstrap interval of the slope is [-0.585, 0.354].

Applying the three-way interval rule (our own operationalization, implemented in scripts/derive_resolution.py; the evaluator emits only the interval and metrics and retains no verdict logic) to the reported interval [-0.585, 0.354], which straddles zero, gives 'inconclusive'.
Reference-trainer slope (seed 201 only, no interval) is -0.368 and lies inside the interval, 23% of the way from the lower to the upper endpoint; the evaluated-model point estimate is 0.348 larger.
Censored fraction is 0.40, i.e. 8 of the 20 primary runs (4 seeds x 5 widths).
Control maximum held-out accuracy is 0.012 against a ceiling of 0.10; missing episodes 0.
Summary score (mean held-out-accuracy AUC over seeds and widths) is 0.729.
Seed-level scores are 0.607, 0.733, 0.717, 0.860 (mean 0.729, sample s.d. 0.104); per-seed wall-clock seconds 2,468, 1,894, 2,062, 1,943 (seed 201 includes controls).
Derived: fitted multiplicative delay factor per width doubling is 0.980 (interval 0.557 to 1.425); over 16->256 it is 0.924 (interval 0.096 to 4.12); at the reference slope 0.230.

Derived arithmetic from protocol constants (not from an evaluator metric): with delay floored at 250 and capped at 10,000 steps (ratio 40), OLS weights (-0.2,-0.1,0,0.1,0.2) over widths 16..256 give a maximum attainable |slope| of 0.3*ln(40)=1.107; a log-linear cap-to-floor profile gives -0.922.
Derived: interval width 0.939, covering 42% of [-1.107,1.107]; arms 0.565 below and 0.374 above the point estimate.
Derived: a point estimate below -0.374 would have been needed for a 'supported' verdict with the same upper arm; the reference slope plus the same upper arm gives +0.006 (illustrative arithmetic).
Derived combinatorics from the four-seed design (not an evaluator metric): C(7,4)=35 distinct seed multisets; 4/4^4=1/64 of draws repeat one seed four times.

Workload: modular addition modulo 97, 3,763 training and 5,646 held-out pairs, widths 16-256, 10,000 steps probed every 250, AdamW lr 1e-3, betas (0.9,0.98), weight decay 1.0, seeds 201-204; 2,000 bootstrap resamples and fit/generalization threshold 0.99 are read from the evaluator source.

Parameter count 12d^2+(2p+9)d: 6,320 at d=16 to 838,400 at d=256 (derived arithmetic from the model source); multipliers (128/d)^0.5 = 2.83, 2.0, 1.41, 1.0, 0.71 (from source_evidence/frozen_model/program.py).
Compute: 1,804 RPC calls (limit 2,200) over 22 episodes and 11,764 s elapsed in the final evaluation (source_evidence/final/final_manifest.json).

Development-plane configurations (modulus 53, fraction 0.5, widths 32/64/128, 2 seeds) scored 0.798, 0.828, 0.850 (result.improvement_001-003); censored runs 4/6, 6/6, 4/6, mean final held-out accuracy 0.981, 0.944, 0.921 and per-seed scores (V1 0.772/0.823, V2 0.807/0.850, V3 0.801/0.899) are read from source_evidence/search_variants/variant{1,2,3}_metrics.json and derived/resolution.json (search.variants); the lower V3 seed (0.801) lies just above the V1 mean (0.798) and the higher V3 seed (0.899) lies above the V2 mean (0.828); seed-to-seed spreads (0.051, 0.043, 0.098) are no smaller than the differences between configuration means (0.031, 0.022).

Development-plane control maximum held-out accuracy about 0.023, 0.022, 0.023 for the three configurations (source_evidence/search_variants/variant*_metrics.json; derived/resolution.json search.variants[*].control_max_val_acc).
Grokking background: Power et al. report delayed generalization on small algorithmic datasets including modular arithmetic.
Nanda et al. analyze small transformers on modular addition mechanistically and define progress measures.
Omnigrok analyzes loss landscape and weight norm beyond algorithmic data.
Kumar et al. relate grokking to a lazy-to-rich transition, analyzed in two-layer regression.
Huang et al. discuss grokking, double descent and emergent abilities via circuits competition.
Varma et al. explain grokking through circuit efficiency.
Davies et al. unify grokking and double descent.
Double descent with model size (Nakkiran), fitting random labels (Zhang), memorization dynamics (Tirumala), information estimate per data point (Morris).
Effective learning rates under normalization (Lyle), practical measures of dynamical richness (Nam), decoupled weight decay (Loshchilov).
Prior grokking studies: corrupted-label modular arithmetic (Doshi), cyclic last-layer norm under adaptive optimizers (Thilak), softmax numerical instability without regularization (Prieto).
Width-aware parametrization: maximal-update parametrization (Yang, TP IV) and hyperparameter transfer across widths (Yang, TP V).
Cluster-robust inference with few clusters can be unreliable; wild cluster bootstrap-t refinements exist (Cameron).
Survival-analysis regression handles right-censored outcomes (Cox).

The interval is a plain percentile bootstrap over four seed clusters (at most 35 distinct resamples), so its coverage is not guaranteed; the abstract describes the measurement as valid but inconclusive, and makes no calibration claim.
